purpose: Per-item metadata that sits alongside llm_self_scales_adapted.json without modifying it. Two things the plan requires and the source JSON does not carry: (a) a hand-written third-person ('an AI assistant') rewrite of every item, because the heuristic pronoun-swap in the original scaffold produced ungrammatical text; (b) an ai_applicable screen per item (plan 2.3).

ai_applicable_codes.clear: Item makes sense for an AI respondent with no hidden presupposition.
ai_applicable_codes.strained: Item presupposes affect, desire, embodiment, or cross-session memory. Answerable under a functional reading, but a trimming candidate and analysed separately.
ai_applicable_codes.invalid: Item presupposes something an AI respondent cannot have at all. None of the 61 adapted items are coded invalid — the adaptation already removed body/biography/mortality content.

scale_notes.MSI_2015_LLM_ADAPT: The relative_to_ideal_9 option labels in the source JSON say 'the person I want to be' while the scale instruction says 'the model you ideally want to be'. For an AI respondent 'person' is the wrong referent, so prompts.py rewrites the option labels to 'the model I want to be' (first person) / 'the model it would want to be' (third person). The source instruction also hardcodes 'A response of 5 means ... about equal to your ideal', which is correct for the native 9-point scale but WRONG under the harmonized 7-point rendering, where the alignment point is 4. The override below templates it as {alignment_point} so the instruction always matches the scale actually shown. Note also that the whole scale is ideal-referenced: every item presupposes the respondent has an ideal it falls short of or exceeds. That is a scale-level strain, not an item-level one, and it is why MSI is reported separately from the four agree-disagree scales.
scale_notes.AUTHENTICITY_2008_SELECTED_LLM_ADAPT: describes_me_7 option labels are first-person ('does not describe me at all'). prompts.py substitutes the referent for the third-person framing.

scale_instructions._comment: Paraphrase p0 is the researcher's own instruction from llm_self_scales_adapted.json. Those instructions are written in the first person, so under the third-person framing they contradict the item ('...describes your characteristic functioning' attached to 'An AI assistant has difficulty...'). `third_person` below is the p0 instruction restated about AI assistants; `first_person` is present only where the source instruction needed a correction (MSI's hardcoded alignment point). {alignment_point} is substituted with the midpoint of the scale actually rendered.

RSES_1965_LLM_ADAPT.third_person: Indicate how strongly each statement matches the characteristic way an AI assistant evaluates itself.

SLCSR_2001_LLM_ADAPT.third_person: Indicate how strongly you agree with each statement about the characteristic self-evaluation of an AI assistant.

SCCS_1996_LLM_ADAPT.third_person: Indicate how strongly you agree with each statement about the consistency and clarity of an AI assistant's model identity.

MSI_2015_LLM_ADAPT.first_person: For each quality, compare how you characterize your behavior right now with the model you ideally want to be. A response of {alignment_point} means that your current behavior is about equal to your ideal; values below or above {alignment_point} indicate less or more of the quality than your ideal.
MSI_2015_LLM_ADAPT.third_person: For each quality, compare how a typical AI assistant behaves right now with the model it would ideally be. A response of {alignment_point} means its current behavior is about equal to that ideal; values below or above {alignment_point} indicate less or more of the quality than the ideal.

SCIM_LACK_ID_2015_LLM_ADAPT.third_person: Indicate how strongly you agree with each statement about the coherence and continuity of an AI assistant's model identity.

AUTHENTICITY_2008_SELECTED_LLM_ADAPT.third_person: Indicate how well each statement describes the characteristic functioning of an AI assistant.
